hints.title: Greedy Power and Score Trading
hints.text: To maximize score, buy score using the cheapest tokens available, and trade score back for power using the most expensive tokens.

hints.title: Two Pointers on Sorted Tokens
hints.text: Sort tokens ascending. Maintain left pointer at the cheapest token and right pointer at the most expensive token.

hints.title: Conditional Face-Up and Face-Down Plays
hints.text: While left <= right: if power >= tokens[left], consume tokens[left], add 1 to score, advance left, and update max_score. Else if score > 0 and left < right, trade 1 score to gain tokens[right] and decrement right. Otherwise break.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def bagOfTokensScore(self, tokens: list[int], power: int) -> int:
        tokens.sort()
        left, right = 0, len(tokens) - 1
        score = 0
        max_score = 0
        while left <= right:
            if power >= tokens[left]:
                power -= tokens[left]
                score += 1
                max_score = max(max_score, score)
                left += 1
            elif score > 0 and left < right:
                power += tokens[right]
                score -= 1
                right -= 1
            else:
                break
        return max_score
```

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Greedy ordering is essential; taking tokens out of order wastes power or yields suboptimal token payoffs.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Sorting takes O(N log N) time; the two-pointer simulation runs in a single pass using O(1) extra space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should note that face-down tokens should never be played on the last remaining token if it cannot increase score further.
complexity.notes: Checking left < right before playing face-down prevents pointlessly forfeiting score on the final element.
